page: Microsoft Azure M128s is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the MS family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 128 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 64 physical Intel Xeon 8280M cores with hyper-threading enabled. Operating at a base frequency of 2.7 GHz, the processor includes a cache hierarchy of 32 KB L1d, 1.0 MB L2, and 38 MB L3 cache. The system is equipped with 2048.0 GB of RAM, providing 16.0 GB of memory per physical core, and includes 4194 GB of local storage with Premium Storage capabilities.

Benchmark data reveals a clear performance tradeoff between single-core and multi-core operations. Single-core metrics, including stress-ng, Geekbench, and single-threaded compression, fall into the bottom 10% tier. Conversely, multi-core performance is strong, placing in the top 25% for stress-ng multi-core, bzip3 decompression, and Passmark CPU tests. Memory bandwidth is exceptionally high, with uncached large-block read and write speeds ranking in the top 10% tier. Database operations and Redis SET performance are also robust, with Redis achieving 80.51 million operations per second.

Given its massive memory capacity and high multi-core throughput, the M128s is highly cost-efficient for memory-intensive enterprise workloads rather than single-threaded tasks. It is well-suited for large-scale databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, and heavy multi-threaded data processing. However, it is less optimal for workloads requiring high single-core performance or real-time LLM text generation, where it exhibits poor performance.
